title: Session 7: The cross

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: The Quran says of Jesus, "they slew him not nor crucified". The Bible's prophets, its eyewitness and its earliest creed say he was crucified, died and rose. Read both, and weigh what each says about its own witnesses.

steps.question: The Quran says "they slew him not nor crucified, but it appeared so unto them". What does Psalm 22 describe, long before?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: and have said, Verily we have slain Christ Jesus the son of Mary, the apostle of GOD; yet they slew him not, neither crucified him, but he was represented by one in his likeness; and verily they who disagreed concerning him were in a doubt as to this matter, and had no sure knowledge thereof, but followed only an uncertain opinion. They did not really kill him; but GOD took him up unto himself: and GOD is mighty and wise.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: And because of their saying: We slew the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, Allah's messenger - they slew him not nor crucified, but it appeared so unto them; and lo! those who disagree concerning it are in doubt thereof; they have no knowledge thereof save pursuit of a conjecture; they slew him not for certain. But Allah took him up unto Himself. Allah was ever Mighty, Wise.

facts.text: "Pierced" in Psalm 22:16 is a disputed word. Most Hebrew copies read ka'ari, like "a lion"; the Greek Septuagint, made before Christ, reads they dug, and a Psalms scroll from Nahal Hever near the Dead Sea reads ka'aru, a form of karah: "properly to dig".
John says the soldiers' casting of lots fulfilled Psalm 22:18: "They parted my raiment among them".
Sale words 4:157 "he was represented by one in his likeness"; Pickthall, "it appeared so unto them". Muslim scholars give different accounts of what this means.

steps.question: What does Isaiah 53 say happened to the servant of the LORD, and why?

facts.text: Wounded is chalal: "properly to bore"; bruised is daka: "to crumble".
Philip read Isaiah 53 with the Ethiopian and "preached unto him Jesus".

steps.question: What does the eyewitness in John 19 say he saw when the soldier pierced Jesus' side, and why does he tell it?

facts.text: Crucified is stauroo: "to impale on the cross". John says "he that saw it bare record, and his record is true".
Writers outside the Bible also say Jesus was put to death: the Roman historian Tacitus (about AD 116) writes that Christus suffered the extreme penalty under Pontius Pilate.

steps.question: The Quran says God took Jesus up unto himself. What did the risen Jesus show his disciples, and how was he taken up?

outside.label: From the Quran: not Scripture
outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: When GOD said, O Jesus, verily I will cause thee to die, and I will take thee up unto me, and I will deliver thee from the unbelievers; and I will place those who follow thee above the unbelievers, until the day of resurrection: then unto me shall ye return, and I will judge between you of that concerning which ye disagree.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: (And remember) when Allah said: O Jesus! Lo! I am gathering thee and causing thee to ascend unto Me, and am cleansing thee of those who disbelieve and am setting those who follow thee above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then unto Me ye will (all) return, and I shall judge between you as to that wherein ye used to differ.

outside.why: The Quran is the holy book of Islam. It is shown here only to set its words beside the Bible, in two public domain translations: one by a Christian scholar, one by a Muslim. It is not Scripture, and no question is answered from it.

texts.name: George Sale (1734)
texts.text: And peace be on me the day whereon I was born, and the day whereon I shall die, and the day whereon I shall be raised to life.

texts.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
texts.text: Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!

facts.text: The Arabic word in 3:55 is mutawaffika. Sale translated it "I will cause thee to die"; Pickthall, "I am gathering thee". Muslim scholars differ on whether it means death or being taken up alive.

In the Quran (19:33) Jesus says "Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive". In Luke he says "handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have".

steps.question: What does Paul say he "received" and delivered first of all, and who saw the risen Jesus?

facts.text: Buried is thapto: "to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter"; rose is egeiro: "to waken". Paul names witnesses who could still be asked: "the greater part remain unto this present".
1 Corinthians was written about AD 55, almost 600 years before the Quran. Many scholars date the creed Paul quotes to within a few years of the cross.

outside_sources.name: George Sale (1734)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation made directly from the Arabic. Sale was a Christian scholar. He did not number the verses; the numbers here are the standard ones.

outside_sources.name: Marmaduke Pickthall (1930)
outside_sources.about: The first English translation by an English Muslim, read by scholars in Cairo before it was printed. Public domain in the US (published 1930) and wherever the term is life plus 70 years (Pickthall died in 1936).
outside_sources.source: The 1930 London printing (George Allen & Unwin), checked word for word; text from Tanzil.net with its slips corrected
